stem: A sequence is defined by $a_1={=c}$ and $a_{n+1}={=m}a_n+{=k}$ for $n\ge 1$. Find $a_2$, $a_3$, $a_4$, estimate the general term $a_n$ as an expression in $n$, and prove your estimate by mathematical induction. Give $a_n$ in terms of $n$.
solution: Add 1 to each term: $a_1+1={=p}$, $a_2+1={=p2}$, $a_3+1={=p3}$, $a_4+1={=p4}$. These are {=p} times powers of {=m}.
Then $a_{k+1}={=m}\left({=p}\cdot{=m}^{k-1}-1\right)+{=k}={=p}\cdot{=m}^{k}-{=m}+{=k}={=p}\cdot{=m}^{k}-1$, which is the formula with $n=k+1$.
By induction the formula holds for all $n\ge 1$: $a_n={=p}\cdot{=m}^{n-1}-1$.
notes:
Recurrence a_{n+1}=m a_n+(m-1) has fixed point -1, so a_n=(c+1)m^(n-1)-1. Only 9 distinct instances (m 3 values, c 3 values).
